(Columbia, South Carolina) | college = * [[Mars Hill Lions men's basketball|Mars Hill]] (2018–2021) * [[Winston-Salem State Rams men's basketball|Winston Salem State]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team1 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | years2 = 2024 | team2 = [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team4 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years5 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team5 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years6 = 2026–present | team6 = [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association|CIAA]] (2022) }} '''Javonte Cooke''' (born July 11, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mars Hill Lions]] and the [[Winston-Salem State Rams men's basketball|Winston-Salem State Rams]]. ==High school career== Cooke graduated from Covenant Classical School in [[Columbia, South Carolina]]. As a senior, he averaged 23 points, 9 rebounds 4.5 steals and 3.5 assists per game. He earned SCISA A Player of the Year. He was Most Outstanding Player in the Georgia vs. South Carolina All Star Game.{{cite web|title=Javonte Cooke|url=https://www.marshilllions.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/cooke_javonte_q2i5?view=bio|work=Mars Hill University Athletics|access-date=September 26, 2024}} ==College career== Cooke enrolled at the [[University of South Carolina Aiken]], but only redshirted as a freshman before transferring.{{cite web|title=Javonte Cooke - Men's Basketball|url=https://pacersports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/javonte-cooke/7914|work=University of South Carolina Aiken Athletics|access-date=September 26, 2024}} ===Mars Hill University=== Cooke played for [[Mars Hill Lions|Mars Hill]] from 2018 to 2021. He played in 47 games during his time at the school and made 27 starts. He averaged 14 points and 5.7 rebounds in two seasons. He reached double figures scoring in 34 games, with nine games over 20 points during the 2019–2020 season.{{cite web|title=Javonte Cooke|url=https://www.marshilllions.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/cooke_javonte_q2i5?view=bio|work=Mars Hill University Athletics|access-date=September 26, 2024}} On November 4, 2020, Cooke was selected to the preseason All-South Atlantic Conference Second Team.{{cite web|title=Cooke tabbed to Preseason All-SAC Second Team|url=https://www.marshilllions.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/releases/20201104gg7tmu|work=Mars Hill University Athletics|date=November 4, 2020|access-date=September 26, 2024}} ===Winston-Salem State=== Cooke joined [[Winston-Salem State Rams men's basketball|Winston-Salem State]] in the Fall of 2021. He played in 23 games for the team and helped them claim the CIAA Southern Division title. He averaged 17.5 points, 3.9 rebounds 1.5 assists and 1.8 steals per game. He finished the season fifth in the conference in scoring, sixth in field goal percentage and first in 3-point field goal percentage and 3-point field goals per game. He was named HBCU Player of the Week and CIAA Player of the Week at least once during the season as well as BOXTOROW National Player of the Week. Cooke was named to the All-CIAA Backcourt Team and CIAA All-Tournament Team. He scored 1,220 points during his career.{{cite web|title=Javonte Cooke - 2021-22 - Men's Basketball|url=https://wssurams.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/javonte-cooke/2696|work=Winston-Salem State University|access-date=September 26, 2024}} In March 2022, Cooke received an invitation to participate in the HBCU All-Star basketball game.{{cite web|title=Javonte Cooke Selected To HBCU All-Star Game|url=https://wssurams.com/news/2022/3/31/3_31_2022_109.aspx|work=Winston-Salem State University|date=March 31, 2022|access-date=September 26, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Iowa Wolves (2022–2024)=== On October 25, 2022, Cooke signed, after a tryout, with the [[Iowa Wolves]] as a prospect.{{cite web|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/iowa-wolves-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=September 28, 2024}} After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Cooke joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|first=Steven J.|last=Gaither|title=Minnesota Timberwolves summer league includes G-Leaguer from HBCU|url=https://hbcugameday.com/2023/07/05/minnesota-timberwolves-summer-league-includes-g-leaguer-from-hbcu/|website=HBCUGameday.com|date=July 5, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2024}} and on October 21, 2023, he signed with the team,{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Brian Bowen II and Javonte Cooke|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-brian-bowen-ii-and-javonte-cooke|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2024}} but was waived the same day.{{cite tweet|author=Timberwolves PR|title=The @Timberwolves have waived Brian Bowen II and Javonte Cook. Minnesota's roster stands at 17 players.|number=1715775917501370465|user=Twolves_PR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2024}} On October 29, he rejoined Iowa.{{cite web|title=Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2024}} ===Brampton Honey Badgers (2024)=== On May 10, 2024, Cooke signed with the [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]],{{cite web|title=Honey Badgers add NBA G League Guard Cooke to Roster|url=https://www.cebl.ca/honey-badgers-add-nba-g-league-guard-cooke-to-roster|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 10, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} but waived him on June 29, in the aftermath of their latest loss against Scarborough.{{cite web|title=New-look Honey Badgers come back to clip Alliance in wild finish|url=https://www.cebl.ca/new-look-honey-badgers-come-back-to-clip-alliance-in-wild-finish|website=CEBL.ca|date=June 29, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2024–2025)=== After joining the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|first=Francisco|last=Manzano|title=Timberwolves Announce NBA 2K25 Summer League 2024 in Las Vegas Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-announce-nba-2k25-summer-league-2024-in-las-vegas-roster|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} Cooke signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on October 11, 2024.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Sign, Waive Javonte Cooke|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/thunder-javonte-cooke-agree-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 12, 2024|access-date=October 12, 2024}} However, he was waived the next day and on October 25, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 11, 2024}} ===Portland Trail Blazers / Rip City Remix (2025–2026)=== On October 20, 2025, Cooke signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Javonte Cooke to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-javonte-cook-to-two-way-contract|access-date=October 25, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On November 20, Cooke made his NBA regular season debut, putting up four points, one assist, and one steal in a 122–121 loss to the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hbcu/former-hbcu-star-makes-nba-debut-in-loss-to-bulls|title=Former HBCU star makes NBA debut in loss to Bulls|website=ClutchPoints|last=Barnes|first=Randall|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 21, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/college/article313006372.html|title=NBA debut for Javonte Cooke breaks HBCU drought|website=The Sacramento Bee|last=Gaither|first=Steven|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 20, 2025}} He made 19 appearances for Portland during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 1.2 points, 1.0 rebound, and 0.4 assists. Cooke was waived by the Trail Blazers on March 2, 2026.{{Cite web|title=Blazers Waive Javonte Cooke|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/trail-blazers-news/109770/portland-trail-blazers-waive-javonte-cooke-nba-g-league-news-two-way-contract|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=blazersedge.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland]] | 19 || 0 || 4.9 || .220 || .130 || 1.000 || 1.0 || .4 || .3 || .0 || 1.2 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 19 || 0 || 4.9 || .220 || .130 || 1.000 || 1.0 || .4 || .3 || .0 || 1.2 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Cooke is the son of Jermaine and Valerie Cooke.
